title: The founder, the ads and the look back
lede: Groupon advertised mostly by email, so there is less film than for a television-era brand. These are the Super Bowl spot that had to be pulled, a news report on the reaction, the founder explaining the model at its peak, a newspaper asking whether the valuation made sense, a later Super Bowl ad and one retrospective.

videos.title: “Save the Money: Tibet,” the Super Bowl XLV spot
videos.caption: Uploaded on February 6, 2011, the day of the game. It opens as an appeal for Tibet and turns into a pitch for a restaurant discount. Groupon apologized and pulled the campaign within the week.[^22]

videos.title: Radio Free Asia: “Super Bowl Stirs Tibet Backlash”
videos.caption: A two-minute news report uploaded on February 7, 2011, the day after the broadcast, on the criticism of the ad.

videos.title: Andrew Mason at DEMO Fall 2010
videos.caption: VentureBeat’s interview with the founder, uploaded September 15, 2010, three months before the reported Google offer.[^21] He describes how Groupon grew out of The Point.

videos.title: The New York Times DealBook: “In Groupon I.P.O., Echo of Tech Bubble?”
videos.caption: Uploaded January 18, 2011. A reporter and an analyst discuss whether Groupon is worth an expected $15 billion, ten months before it listed at a first-day value of $16.7 billion.[^23]

videos.title: “Who Wouldn’t,” the 2018 Super Bowl spot with Tiffany Haddish
videos.caption: Groupon’s return to the Super Bowl, seven years after the Tibet ad. This copy was uploaded by a viewer on February 19, 2018; the airing year is from the uploader’s title.

videos.title: Company Man: “The Decline of Groupon...What Happened?”
videos.caption: A thirteen-minute independent retrospective. YouTube lists it as about three years old; we could not read the exact upload date, so the year is approximate. Its figures are the uploader’s; ours are in the sections above.

note: Upload dates were read from each video’s YouTube page on October 3, 2026.
